title: Region-bridge failover automation for Private VPC: orchestration, upgrades, and health verification
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Summary:
Build an automated, repeatable failover orchestration for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments that bridges traffic between primary and secondary regions (region-bridge), automates upgrade/rollback during drills, and validates application-level health and model-serving correctness before declaring a failover complete.

Scope and goals:
- Provide a Terraform-first IaC pattern (reusable modules + orchestration layer) to create the bridging infrastructure needed for cross-region failovers for Private deployments.
- Automate control-plane upgrade choreography (preflight checks, staged rollout, verification hooks, and automated rollback) to be used during drills and real incidents.
- Implement a health-verification suite that tests model-serving correctness (KV cache hydration, prefix-caching verification, request/response validation), performance SLOs, and data-plane consistency.
- Produce a runbook and GitHub Actions workflow to run scheduled drills with minimal manual steps and integrated observability (dashboards + PagerDuty).

Technical approach and design decisions:
- Terraform modules: extract and publish the following modules in the private-infra repo: vpc-peering-bridge, route-propagation, nat-and-egress-policy, controlplane-kms-roles. These modules are parameterized by region, account, and cidr block.
- Orchestration: GitHub Actions + Terraform Cloud remote runs; orchestration layer sequences: plan -> preflight-tests -> apply -> canary-bridge -> verification-tests -> promote -> cleanup. Use Terraform workspaces per-customer to isolate state.
- Upgrade strategy: staged control-plane upgrade using a region-bridge proxy: bootstrap secondary region with same runtime version, warm KV caches via synthetic traffic, then flip traffic gradually (10%, 50%, 100%) using the bridge proxy. If degradation detected revert to previous control-plane snapshot.
- State management: keep remote state in Terraform Cloud; snapshots of critical state (service config, routing) taken to S3-compatible backup before any apply.
- Health checks: implement three layers of checks: infra-level (route propagate, peering status), service-level (instance readiness, model-kernel compatibility), and functional-level (end-to-end inference tests using a canonical prompt set). Functional tests run with golden prompts and assert logits/token patterns within tolerance.
- Observability: temporary drill dashboards created via Grafana templated dashboard (latency, token throughput, error rates, model divergence metrics). Alerts tied to PagerDuty escalation policy for drills.
- Security: cross-account IAM roles use least privilege; all cross-region data egress paths documented and approved. Security review required before production drills.

Progress updates and work done so far:
- Week 2026-02-12: Module extraction PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/private-infra/pull/462. Initial vpc-peering-bridge + route-propagation modules implemented, unit tests added.
- Week 2026-02-19: Orchestration prototype (GitHub Actions) implemented in repo: https://github.com/redwood/private-ops/actions/workflows/region-bridge.yml (branch: eng/region-bridge/orchestrator).
- Week 2026-02-25: Preflight test harness (k6 + lightweight Go runner) created and validated against staging. PR: https://github.com/redwood/private-tests/pull/28.
- Week 2026-03-05: First staged drill executed in staging->canary region (staging-us-west2 -> staging-eu-west1). Drill executed via workflow in a maintenance window; control-plane upgrade + 10% traffic flip validated by automated tests. No data-loss; KV cache warm-up reduced token latency by ~12%. Drill logs: https://logs.redwood.dev/collections/region-bridge/2026-03-05.
- Week 2026-03-10: Integration PR for verification hooks and rollback scripts opened: https://github.com/redwood/private-ops/pull/199 (adding canary-promote/rollback actions).

Test results and metrics from staging drill (2026-03-05):
- End-to-end success rate for golden prompts: 99.3% (target >99%).
- Median token latency change during 10% flip: +9ms. During 50% flip: +22ms (still within SLO of 150ms).
- Model output divergence metric (KL proxy): within acceptable tolerance for 97% of prompts.
- KV cache warm-up time (to reach 90% hit rate): ~45s after synthetic warm-up traffic.

Open issues and blockers:
- IAM cross-account role provisioning for customer-managed accounts is blocked by legal on egress/data transfer terms. Ticket with Legal created: LGL-1143.
- Some customers use strict private endpoints that do not allow automated outbound synth traffic; need per-customer adapters or a manual warm-up path.
- Need SRE on-call coverage sign-off and a scheduled maintenance window before running production drills.

Risk mitigations and fallbacks:
- Automated rollback scripts that restore previous control-plane snapshot and re-establish original routing in under N+5 minutes.
- If synthetic warm-up unavailable, we fallback to KV cache seed snapshots (stored encrypted) and perform gradual traffic ramp only after checksum validation.

Next milestones (short term):
- 2026-03-20: Complete security review and obtain sign-off (security_review_required = true).
- 2026-03-24: Run a dry-run failure drill on one pilot customer in dedicated staging environment with SRE on-call and Product observer.
- 2026-03-31: Extend orchestration to support blue/green control-plane upgrades and test rollback latency under synthetic load.
- 2026-04-01: Draft customer-facing runbook and post-mortem template in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DR/Region+Bridge+Runbook.

Acceptance criteria (to close):
- Terraform modules published to private-infra with automated tests and >=80% module coverage.
- Orchestration workflow supports end-to-end plan/apply/verify/rollback and can be executed with a single GH Actions trigger.
- Runbook with DR checklist, SRE playbook, and customer notice templates published and reviewed.
- One successful production-simulated drill on a pilot customer with verified metrics and no customer data-loss.
